questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Conditional sentences of the first type
questions.stem: In a study group, a student writes: 'If it rains, we will stay home.' What type of conditional is this?

options.misconception: confuses a specific future with a general truth

questions.explanation: A real future condition with 'if + present, will + verb' is first type. The others describe hypothetical or general patterns.
questions.hint: Check the tense in the if-clause.

provenance.author: bank-team-spanish
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Conditional sentences of the second type
questions.stem: Which sentence is a second-type conditional?

options.text: 'If I have time, I will revise.'
'If I had more time, I would revise.'
'If I had had time, I would have revised.'

questions.explanation: Second type uses 'if + past, would + verb' for a hypothetical present. The others are first, third, or zero type.
questions.hint: Look for past in the if-clause and would in the result.

provenance.author: bank-team-spanish
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Conditional sentences of the third type
questions.stem: Which sentence is a third-type conditional?

options.text: 'If I had studied, I would have passed.'

questions.explanation: Third type uses 'if + past perfect, would have + past participle' for an unreal past. The others are first, second, or zero type.
questions.hint: Look for past perfect and would have.

provenance.author: bank-team-spanish
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: The imperfect subjunctive
questions.stem: In a study note, 'Si yo ___ más tiempo, repasaría.' Which form completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: 'Tuviera' is the imperfect subjunctive needed after 'si' in a second-type conditional. The others are indicative or future.
questions.hint: Use the imperfect subjunctive after si.

provenance.author: bank-team-spanish
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: SPANISH

answer.exemplar: First conditionals are real future possibilities; second are hypothetical present situations; third are unreal past events.

questions.explanation: The three types differ in time and reality. First is real future, second hypothetical present, third unreal past.
